title: Soveraeign Federation Crossing
description: One record offered across the boundary between two sovereign nodes, and what the receiving node did about it. A crossing carries an address and a digest, never authority and never standing: whatever standing the record holds in the node that offered it, the record a receiving node admits enters that node at RECORDED and climbs only through that node's own transitions (decisions/0039). Nothing here transports bytes; a crossing names content the two nodes address the same way.

from_node.description: The node that offered the record.

to_node.description: The node the record was offered to. Exactly one of from_node and to_node is the node holding this crossing; scripts/sovkernel/federation.py checks that against the node registry.

origin_seat.description: The seat in the offering node that produced the record. Carried so a reader can attribute the offer. It is not a seat in the receiving node and confers nothing there.

record_kind.description: What kind of record is offered, e.g. thread, post, asset-version.

standing_at_origin.description: What the record stands at in the node that offered it. Reported, never inherited. A receiving node reads this as a claim about somewhere else.

admission.description: The receiving node's settlement of this offer, or null while the offer is unsettled. A node may only fill this in for a crossing addressed to it; a peer's settlement of an outbound offer is the peer's record and cannot be held here as settled.

admitted_by.description: The local seat that settled the offer. Admitting a peer's record is a judgement, so this must be the receiving node's root seat.

outcome.description: Receipt vocabulary. COMMITTED created a local record; REFUSED created none; COUNTERED created a counter-record against a local record this offer contradicts.

local_record_address.description: The record this node created. Present for COMMITTED and COUNTERED, null for REFUSED.

local_standing.description: What the local record stands at on creation. The enum has one non-null member on purpose: a crossing cannot deliver a record above RECORDED, whatever it stood at in the offering node. Null when nothing local was created.
